The Vendetta Gazette

Vol. XXI • August 31, 2026 • “All the Blood That’s Fit to Print” • Two Cents (If You’re Still Alive to Pay)

★ TERRITORY GAINS THIS WEEK ★ Wu-Tang             +163 turfs
Flattop              +85 turfs
Charle Reborn       +3 turfs
Claude               +3 turfs

Wu-Tang Continues His Reign of Organised Terror; Sir Caprice Utterly Consumed — Again

One Hundred and Sixty-Three Turfs Added to an Already Grotesque Empire; The Iron Fist Yawns; Sir Caprice Weeps By Our Man in the Trenches, Ignatius P. Flambeau

This correspondent, having last week solemnly shattered his own vow never to open another dispatch with the name Wu-Tang, now finds himself in the even more undignified position of doing precisely that for the fourth consecutive week. Colleagues at rival publications have suggested he simply pre-set the headline in moveable type and leave it bolted to the press indefinitely. The suggestion, it must be confessed, has considerable merit.

Wu-Tang, the Iron Fist of the East Side, has added yet another one hundred and sixty-three turfs to his already staggering territorial dominion, executing one hundred and sixty-six separate captures and — in a demonstration of almost contemptuous financial efficiency — conducting eighty-three simultaneous raids upon the devastated holdings of one Sir Caprice, stripping that wretched gentleman of cash and weapons to the reported value of some $55,681 in coin and 55,049 units of ordnance. Sir Caprice, who last week endured an identical catastrophe at the same iron hands, appears by all credible intelligence to have been rendered, in the technical underworld parlance, absolutely and comprehensively cleaned out. Whether the man retains sufficient resources to purchase a bus ticket out of Vendetta City is, at press time, unknown. Whether he possesses the dignity to use it is another question entirely.

Sources close to the Iron Fist report that Wu-Tang's organisation moves with the eerie precision of a machine that has long since ceased to require human emotion. One hundred and sixty-six territorial assaults upon a single target — eighty-three paired with plunder, the remainder cold, surgical captures — delivered across seven days with the monotonous regularity of a factory whistle. The map of Vendetta City, this correspondent is sorry to report, increasingly resembles a document bearing Wu-Tang's personal monogram.

Flattop, the Headhunter of the Back Alleys, Delivers a Week of Spectacular Obliteration

Six Headquarters Stormed and Seized in Five Days; Five Bosses Eliminated; One Newcomer Stakes His Claim With Startling Violence By Our Man in the Trenches, Ignatius P. Flambeau

If Wu-Tang represents the grinding, inexorable conquest of a continent, then Flattop — the name already whispered with reverence and considerable terror in the meaner precincts of Vendetta City — represents something altogether more surgical and, frankly, more exciting. Where the Iron Fist devours, Flattop decapitates.

In a streak of audacious violence that began on the eighteenth of August and concluded, bloodily, on the twenty-fourth, Flattop stormed and seized no fewer than six enemy headquarters in the span of a single working week. The roll call of the fallen reads like the obituary column of a particularly unlucky neighbourhood: edit (HQ seized, Monday), reccc (HQ seized, Tuesday), Kamog (HQ seized, Thursday), and the thoroughly luckless JasonF, whose headquarters was stormed not once but twice in a single Saturday — a humiliation so complete that one struggles to find appropriate language. JasonD rounded out the carnage on Sunday, his command post falling on the final day of the week like the last domino in a very expensive set.
